questions.title: Preserve a bounded admission contract
questions.prompt: Complete Admission. submit accepts values from 0 through 100 while count is below its capacity. Return false for invalid values or a full queue without changing count. The model is single-threaded. size() reports accepted submissions.
questions.signature: class Admission: bool submit(int value); std::size_t size() const

tests.label: Valid submission
tests.hint: Increase the count only after acceptance.

tests.label: Capacity is enforced
tests.hint: Full means count is already at the limit.

hints: A failed call must leave count_ unchanged.
questions.explanation: Admission is a small failure boundary: a caller sees either acceptance with a state change, or rejection with the old state preserved. Concurrent callers would need additional synchronization.

questions.title: Retry only eligible failures
questions.prompt: attempt is the one-based number of the attempt that just failed. Return true only if the failure is transient and another attempt is available below maxAttempts. Return false for attempt < 1 or maxAttempts < 1.
questions.signature: bool shouldRetry(int attempt, bool transient, int maxAttempts)

tests.label: Another attempt remains
tests.hint: There is one remaining attempt after attempt two.

tests.label: Last allowed attempt
tests.hint: Use a strict comparison at the limit.

tests.label: Permanent failure
tests.hint: A retry budget does not make every failure transient.

tests.label: Invalid numbering
tests.hint: The first valid attempt number is one.

hints: Write the conditions as independent boolean rules.
A retry is available only when attempt < maxAttempts.
questions.explanation: This policy separates “may another attempt help?” from “is the retry budget exhausted?” It does not itself repeat a request or make an operation idempotent.
questions.chapterTitle: Containing Failure with Retries, Circuit Breakers, and Bulkheads

questions.title: Apply a request key once
questions.prompt: Complete IdempotentCounter. apply(key, delta) changes the total only the first time a nonempty key appears and returns true. Reusing a key returns false without changing total. Reject an empty key with std::invalid_argument. Inputs keep every total in int range. This is an in-memory, single-threaded model, not durable distributed storage.
questions.signature: class IdempotentCounter: bool apply(const std::string& key, int delta); int total() const

tests.label: First request applies
tests.hint: Store both the key and the new total.

tests.label: Duplicate does not apply
tests.hint: The key determines duplication, even if its delta changes.

tests.label: Different keys
tests.hint: Distinct keys may both update the total.

tests.label: Empty key rejected
tests.hint: Reject an empty key before touching state.

hints: insert(...).second tells you whether the key was new.
Return false before adding the delta when the key already exists.
questions.explanation: Remembering completed keys prevents repeated effects in this process. A production design also needs atomic persistence, retention rules, and concurrency control.
